Below is a short summary you can paste into the questionnaire; the attachments contain configuration snippets and flow-log screenshots. If you need raw pcap we can provide a sanitized capture under NDA.

Summary (copyable):
- Interconnect and handshake model: Redwood uses mutual TLS for all inter-service and interconnect links. Each service instance holds a short-lived leaf certificate issued by our internal CA (automated with HashiCorp Vault PKI). Certificates rotate automatically every 24 hours for runtime identities and every 7 days for long-lived node certs; revocation is via short CRL windows and OCSP endpoints published to the control plane. Mutual authentication is enforced at the transport layer; accidental plaintext is not permitted between Redwood nodes.

- Tenant isolation and segmentation:
  - Logical tenancy is enforced by a two-tier model: network-level segmentation (per-tenant VPCs or project-scoped subnets) and per-request enforcement with a transparent sidecar proxy that performs token-level authorization and service allowlists.
  - Security groups / firewall rules default to deny and are templated by deployment class (hosted, dedicated, private). Cross-tenant routing requires explicit allow policies and is logged.

- Egress controls and bastionless model:
  - We support a managed egress gateway with outbound allowlists on per-tenant basis; customers can also supply their own NAT/egress appliances in Private deployments.
  - For hosted workloads we operate an egress fleet that performs TLS termination only for telemetry aggregation and then re-establishes mTLS to destination endpoints where required (no HTTPS interception of customer payload).
  - Access to internal admin interfaces is via an authenticated control plane; we avoid standing bastions by using short-lived admin sessions (time-limited credentials + ephemeral jump tokens) and just-in-time access workflows integrated with SSO and MFA.

- Audit and detection:
  - Flow logs (VPC Flow + sidecar connection traces) are retained for 365 days for enterprise customers; default retention is 90 days for self-serve plans.
  - AuthN/AuthZ events and certificate issuance logs are shipped to the centralized audit stream and are tamper-evident (append-only with periodic hashing).
  - We can produce a redacted pcap and connection matrix for your reviewers under an NDA.

Attachments included: network-diagram-v3.png (annotated interconnect flows), egress-proof-points.pdf (screenshots and config snippets).
